subject.title: feat(mcp): stage binary tool content for relay

question: Should OpenClaw accept a process-local host-owned MCP media registry as the trust boundary for relaying staged MCP binary content, with native channel proof deferred to follow-up?
rationale: The implementation changes how external MCP-origin tool results can pass local media paths into channel delivery, and that trust boundary plus proof scope is a maintainer/product-security choice rather than a mechanical correctness issue.

options.title: Rebase and require focused channel proof
options.body: Have the contributor rebase onto current main, preserve the safe MCP filter helper, and add Telegram or another native-channel proof before merge.

options.title: Accept shared-seam proof only
options.body: Merge after rebase based on the MCP stdio seam proof and explicitly track native channel attachment proof as follow-up work.

options.title: Pause for broader API design
options.body: Hold this PR and require a fuller channel attachment/hook API direction before allowing MCP binary relay into core.

recommendation.title: Rebase and require focused channel proof
recommendation.body: Have the contributor rebase onto current main, preserve the safe MCP filter helper, and add Telegram or another native-channel proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision sits at the delivery/media trust boundary where recent history points most strongly to this owner path.
